site_name: One Data Center America ONT-2, 3833 Ebony St, Ontario CA 91761
verification: The article (sponsored Partner Content, dated 2019-10-04, titled "New Data Center Now Open in the Inland Empire") does support that the operator's SECOND Ontario facility had its grand opening in 2019. What is missing is a non-directory page tying that second facility to 3833 Ebony St. Circumstantial support: the operator site lists only one address (3833 Ebony Street) and advertises a 110-foot telecommunications tower, which the article attributes to the newly opened second facility. Against: the operator site carries a 2012 copyright line, implying an earlier first facility whose address I could not find, and a sole contact address could be either building. If 3833 Ebony were the first facility, 2019 would be wrong by several years, so I left it unverified. If the study accepts the directory's ONT-2 label as the site name, 2019 would be supportable from this article. web.archive.org was unavailable to the fetch tool, so I could not check the pre-2019 contact address. Quote was relayed by the fetch tool's summarizer as the opening of the article's first sentence; the researcher's quote matches it.

lead.year_evidence_quote: just had the grand opening of its second data center facility in Ontario, California
lead.notes: A sponsored 'Partner Content' item dated 2019-10-04 reports the grand opening of One Data Center America's second Ontario facility, placed near the 10/15 freeway interchange. The page gives no street address. I tied it to 3833 Ebony only because Baxtel (name hint only, not evidence) labels 3833 Ebony as ONT-2 and a different site as ONT-1. So the 2019 date rests on that unconfirmed link and the item is promotional. No operator page was reachable.

site_name: 274 Brannan St, San Francisco (Swig Company telecom building; now Fortress SF1)
verification: The owner's page does state the 1982 conversion, but to a telecom switching building, not a data center. The same page treats data center tenancy as a later step (it describes the move into data center tenants as a natural progression, undated) and says "Additional upgrades were performed in 2010 to meet the increasing demand for data center space." So the page supports 1982 as the start of telecom-switching use and supports data center use by 2010 at the latest, but gives no year for when data center operation began. The 2008-01-14 REBusiness article calls it a "data and telecommunications building" at 274 Brannan St. and says it was converted from office use to a fiber-rich telecommunications facility, with no conversion date. No page opened dates the Fortress SF1 opening. If the study chooses to treat telecom-switching use as the start of operation, 1982 is supported by the owner's statement (operator_statement); I did not make that definitional call.

lead.year_evidence_quote: 274 Brannan was converted into a telecom switching building in 1982.
lead.notes: Swig's own property page (page now marked SOLD) says the 1923 building became a telecom switching building in 1982. That is a carrier/telecom facility, not clearly a data center, so 1982 is the telecom start and the date the building began operating as a data center is not established. A 2008 trade article (dated 2008-01-14) describes it as a fiber-rich telecom facility but gives no conversion date. Fortress SF1 data center opening date was not found on any non-directory page.

lead.notes: GAO-03-205 (January 2003), which I opened, places the San Mateo IT Center at 2700 Campus Drive and says the building was constructed in 1976 and bought by the Postal Service in 1983. It does not say when the IT center began operating, and the building was not shown to be built as a data center, so I left the year null.
